description: A UTF-8 lead byte followed by an ASCII letter is accepted as part of an identifier
notes: This is a hashicorp/hcl bug: the spec says invalid UTF-8 is always a parse error, and the byte C4 must be followed by a continuation byte. The identifier tables in hclsyntax/unicode_derived.rl, generated by unicode2ragel.rb, allow any byte after some lead bytes (entries such as 0xC4..0xC5 0x00..0xFF and 0xC3 0xB8..0xFF), so the Ident rule in scan_tokens.rl reads C4 and "y" as one character. The bug is wider than this input: [for x\xC3\xFF in [1]: 2] is accepted too, and in x\xC4= the equals sign becomes part of the name. Using the same bytes for the variable and the result shows they form one consistent name, which doesn't appear in the output.
